messages:
sam (Support): FYI — Acme hit a bunch of 500s on /v1/generate at ~15:23 UTC. They say there are no request IDs in their app logs. Can we send a concise ask to get a correlator/trace so we can pull the backend trace?

maya (SRE): Ask for three things, short and actionable: 1) a single curl (or HAR) that reproduces the error, 2) any SDK/device logs around the time, 3) the exact local timestamp + timezone. Also ask them to redact tokens if needed but keep headers. :folded_hands:

sam (Support): Here's a minimal message we can paste to customer: "Can you share (A) one failing curl with `-v` (response headers included) or a HAR export, (B) SDK / device logs around the failure, and (C) the local timestamp? If any header looks like `x-redwood-request-id` or `x-rw-span` please paste it. Redact only the token value."

liam (Mobile Eng): Add mobile tips: Android: `adb logcat | grep -i redwood` (or search for "correlator" / "requestId"). iOS: enable verbose logging `Redwood.setLogLevel(.debug)` and reproduce; share last ~50 lines. If they used our embedded SDK, the console often prints `rw-req=` or `correlator=`.

maya (SRE): If they can't produce a curl, a HAR is the next best thing — Chrome DevTools > Network > right click > Save as HAR with content. Important: include the failing request row and the server response headers.

sam (Support): Paste this curl example for them to adapt (tell them to redact the token):

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "User-Agent: acme/1.2.3" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-35b","input":"test"}'
```

sam (Support): When they run that, ask them to paste the full response headers block (we're specifically looking for headers named like `x-redwood-request-id`, `x-session-id`, `x-rw-span`, or any `x-*` that looks correlator-related). If none present, tell them to also share the raw body.

maya (SRE): Quick proxy check note to include: if the request goes through a corporate proxy or CDN, headers can be stripped. Ask them to run a simple echo test through the same path: `curl -I -H "x-rw-test:1" https://their-proxy/...` and confirm the header makes it to the upstream.

liam (Mobile Eng): For Android repro snippet to include in request: look for `Log.d("Redwood", "rw-req-id=" + response.header("x-redwood-request-id"))` — if their app logs that we can tie their client trace to our backend trace.

sam (Support): Also ask for a tiny minimal reproducible payload (<=5KB). If the issue is streaming, ask them to capture the final stream chunk and the event order.

maya (SRE): If they cannot share auth, that's fine — they should replace the token with `Bearer <REDACTED>` but we need the rest of headers intact (user-agent, content-type, any custom headers).

ops-bot: :information_source: Escalation ticket created #ES-4826 — include the thread_ts for correlation.

sam (Support): TL;DR for copy/paste to customer: "Please send: 1) one failing curl with `-v` (or a HAR export) — include full response headers; 2) SDK/device logs around the timestamp; 3) local timestamp (ISO) and whether the request was proxied; 4) a minimal repro payload. Redact tokens only. If you see any header named like `x-redwood-request-id` / `x-session-id` / `x-rw-span` please paste it exactly."

maya (SRE): I'm available to join the call if they can do a live repro. If they paste curl/HAR into the ticket, I'll start searching traces from our side using the timestamp and UA.

liam (Mobile Eng): If they share an Android/iOS binary trace we can often pull the correlator from the SDK's HTTP layer. Remind them to include device model and OS version.

sam (Support): Adding a tiny config snippet customers can add to JS SDK to log request ids: 

```
client.on('response', (res) => console.log('rw-req-id', res.headers['x-redwood-request-id'] || res.headers['x-session-id']))
```

sam (Support): I'll send the copy now and update the ticket once they reply. Thanks all.
